content_plan.quick-dinner: A complete weeknight dinner built around one hero ingredient that comes together fast. Slide 1: hero shot of the finished dish plated beautifully — rich colour, glossy sauce, clean surface, pure food photography with absolutely no text, numbers, or labels anywhere on the image. Slide 2: flat-lay of raw ingredients loosely arranged by colour — purely photographic, nothing annotated. Slides 3–4: two-beat visual sequence showing one key technique moment (e.g. a vigorous sear, sauce reducing in pan) followed by the finished plated result — no text overlays of any kind. Final slide: tight close-up of texture and colour detail that makes the dish feel craveable and achievable. ALL ingredient quantities, timing, steps, swaps, and any written information belong in the caption only.
content_plan.marinade: One complete marinade built around a single protein or seasonal occasion. Slide 1: hero shot of the marinated, deeply coloured, glistening protein on a clean dark or neutral surface — pure food photography, zero text, numbers, or labels anywhere on the image. Slide 2: aesthetic flat-lay of raw marinade ingredients grouped loosely by colour and texture — purely photographic, nothing annotated. Slides 3–4: visual process contrast — protein submerging into the marinade, then the vivid colour and sheen transformation after marinating — no overlaid text or graphics of any kind. Final slide: finished plated dish in warm directional light, garnished but not cluttered. ALL ratios, quantities, timing, substitution tips, and step information belong in the caption exclusively.
content_plan.technique: One foundational cooking technique relevant to home cooks — e.g. how to build a fond, reverse-sear, bloom spices, or emulsify a pan sauce. Slide 1: hero shot of the dramatic visual payoff of the technique (e.g. a perfectly seared crust, a glossy emulsified sauce) — pure food photography, zero text, numbers, labels, or graphics anywhere on the image. Slide 2: flat-lay or close-up of the key tools or ingredients that make the technique work — purely photographic, nothing annotated. Slides 3–4: two-beat before/after visual sequence showing the technique mid-action and the finished result — no text overlays of any kind. Final slide: close-up detail of the texture, colour, or finish that makes the result unmistakably worth the technique. ALL explanations, ratios, timing, troubleshooting tips, and step-by-step instructions belong in the caption exclusively.

caption_strategy: Because sends and saves are zero across all 22 posts, captions must now do the heavy lifting to trigger those behaviours. Open every caption with a single punchy hook sentence that names the dish or technique and the concrete benefit (e.g. 'This 20-minute soy-ginger marinade triples the flavour of any thigh'). Write the full recipe or technique walkthrough in the caption body — real quantities, exact timing, swap options — so the post is genuinely useful and save-worthy without the reader needing to click anywhere else. End every caption with an explicit, low-friction CTA that targets sends or saves: 'Save this before you shop' or 'Send this to whoever needs a fast dinner tonight'. Use keyword-rich natural language throughout (ingredient names, cuisine style, occasion) because Instagram indexes caption text for search; avoid vague phrases like 'this recipe' with no context. Keep total length 150–300 words.
hashtag_strategy: Use exactly 3–5 hashtags per post, placed at the end of the caption after a line break. Prioritise mid-size niche hashtags (100k–2M posts) over mega tags: e.g. #marinaderecipe, #weeknightdinner, #cookingtechnique, #homecooking, #saucegame. Rotate one hashtag per post to test which drives non-follower reach. Avoid generic mega tags (#food, #recipe) — they bury young accounts. Never put hashtags in comments; in-caption placement signals relevance to Instagram's search index. Reassess in 4 weeks once per-hashtag reach data accumulates.
learnings: All 22 posts show zero sends, saves, and follows — reach is landing almost exclusively on existing connections (avg 1.3–2.0), meaning the algorithm has not yet pushed content to non-followers. The account is in cold-start mode. Priority shift: caption utility is now the single most important lever — write full, genuinely useful recipes/techniques inline so followers have a concrete reason to save or share. Retire the 'sauce' theme (6 posts, reach 1.5, bottom performer) — consolidate effort on quick-dinner, marinade, and technique. Drop w0-19 (reach 1.3) and w6-10 (reach 1.0) slots. Hold cadence at 4/week; do not increase until saves or sends register above zero.
